0.comment: Dori: Kaveh and the Palace of Alcazarzaray
0.content: Dori hired the Kshahrewar architect Kaveh to build her a large, extravagant private estate and gave him a free hand on style. Kaveh did not know the famous "Lord Sangemah Bay" was Dori until they met. He persuaded her to move the site to a cliff in the northern mountains; when the work was seventy percent done, the Withering destroyed it overnight. Dori, furious, ordered him off the project and asked who would bear the losses. Kaveh sold the house his parents had left him and put in his savings to cover seventy percent, she covered the rest, and overspending left him deep in her debt. She saw he was paying for his ideals, not for her, and let him. He still pays her monthly.

1.content: No one knows how Dori met the travelling mage Alice, but they are ideal partners. Alice sends inventions; Dori sells them and ships Alice's share to the safe zone nearest wherever she is, paying labour, shipping and insurance, even in advance. "I, Dori, never default on payment." On the day they met, Dori promised to be Alice's greatest business partner. Alice was her first investor. She is no longer Dori's only supplier, but her payment is always top priority.

2.comment: Dori: The Jinni in the lamp
2.content: Dori's lamp holds a Jinni that was tricked into entering it and never left. She summons it in battle and grants its wishes afterwards; the Jinni sometimes thinks the fairy tale got things backwards. Dori's own story of how she got it: a merchant caught by a Fog Div told it of a "Genie of Beauty and Kindness" who became her supplier, and persuaded the div that it could gain the same power by entering her lamp. Asked if it is true, she charges another 990,000 Mora for "backstory details".

3.comment: Dori: The elder sister and the Vision
3.content: Dori and her elder sister were inseparable, picking flowers, crossing creeks and sliding down dunes together. The elder began coughing blood. Doctors came and went; she always smiled and said she just needed rest. Dori found a crumpled prescription for herbs costing tens of millions of Mora, far beyond the family, and resolved to make a fortune so her family would never again swallow their pain behind smiles. It is implied her Vision came then. "There's nothing that Lord Sangemah Bay cannot achieve."

4.comment: Dori: Canned Knowledge in Port Ormos (3.0)
4.content: In 3.0 Dori was a hidden dealer of illegal Canned Knowledge in Port Ormos, meeting only clients vetted by her informant Raunak and keeping clear of the matra. Alhaitham, blacklisted by her, sent the Traveler and Paimon as "safe" outlanders. They passed her test by outrunning the matra. She sold them capsules and an upsold "million-Mora" capsule that proved nearly worthless. Two days later she sold them intel: the Divine Knowledge Capsule had gone to Mizri, leader of Ayn Al-Ahmar, and she had photographed the deal with a Kamera. Alhaitham called it a very bold move.

5.comment: Dori: The smuggling case and the Court of Desolation (3.1)
5.content: In Cyno's Story Quest, the Traveler kept Dori's name from Cyno, so she shared what she knew. She had quit Canned Knowledge because the smugglers flooded the market and regulations tightened. She warned of its dangers: flawed knowledge is hard to unlearn, and overuse dulls thinking. She guessed the smuggling was a cover for an auction tied to the Court of Desolation, then sold a "Limited Edition Desert Travel Kit" with a map to it and billed the expense to Cyno.

6.comment: Dori: Nefer and the Curatorium of Secrets
6.content: Nefer, a fellow Sumeran and boss of the Curatorium of Secrets in Nod-Krai, rescued Dori when the kuuvahki knocked out her Jinni. Dori gave her thirty percent off everything ever since. She first warned the Traveler away from the Curatorium as a ruinously expensive rival with a temper; she later admitted she simply resented not having Nefer in her debt. Nefer reads her motives effortlessly, which unsettles her.
